transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-25 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~42m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood), Sara Morales (Lumen Head of Data), Dr. Kevin Wu (CTO), Ravi Desai (Infra), Maya Singh (Security)

Summary: quick console tour showing route-level dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, and how to filter by model/version; then discussion on pilot metrics and security requirements.

00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we promised a short console walkthrough today focused on usage analytics and cost breakdown, um before I hand it over to Priya any quick notes on timeline from Lumen?
00:28 Sara Morales: Yeah thanks Alex, we have a Q3 target to launch internal clinical summarization. Pilot needs to run in July and we'd like to understand per-route cost, also which routes we should put on Dedicated vs Hosted, and we'll need security answers for PHI handling.
00:45 Priya Patel: Great, yeah i'll jump straight into the console, can everyone see my screen? I'm on the Usage Analytics page — note that some of the labels on this export can be slightly off, the transcriber sometimes says KV cash instead of cache, so if you see odd terms that's why.
01:12 Dr. Kevin Wu: We can see it. Can you show per-route breakdowns? We have 3 main routes: triage, summarize, eligibility-check.
01:30 Priya Patel: Yep; so here is the per-route dashboard — each route gets a timeseries of requests, median latency, p50/p95, and token counts. The cost model ties token counts to the model / quantization profile and hardware. For example you can see the summarize route spikes on weekdays at 10 AM.
02:05 Jordan Lee: Also we attach model tags so you can compare rlm-2.7b-quant vs rlm-7b-fp16 and see unit cost differences.
02:28 Sara Morales: That's helpful. On the triage route we expect lots of short requests, so cost per-req matters but latency is critical too. How do we balance batching vs latency?
03:03 Priya Patel: Right — Console Optimize tab suggests batching policies based on actual latency SLOs. You can set per-route policies: prefer latency, prefer cost, or balanced. If you choose prefer latency the runtime will reduce batching and favor low-latency kernels; cost will batch more aggressively and use cached prefixes.
03:50 Ravi Desai: Quick Q on caching — we log a lot of prefixes, how does the prefix/KV cache life affect memory on Dedicated nodes?
04:14 Priya Patel: Good question. Cache retention is configurable and the dashboard shows cache hit ratio per route; on Dedicated you can set a cap per instance. In the console we show estimated memory for KV cache and the impact on throughput; the numbers are approximate but we've found they track within 10-15% of real usage in our benchmarks.
05:00 Alex Chen: A few points on cost: the cost breakdown you see here attribs token-level spend to route + model. We also show a predictive monthly run rate based on last 30 days. One common confusion is that embeddings vs generation cost differently — the console separates those.
05:40 Sara Morales: Can we export per-route cost to our finance system? CSV or API?
05:48 Priya Patel: Yes — export CSV and there is an Audit API you can call to pull route-level daily cost. We can add a sample script to your repo.
06:10 Maya Singh: Security: we need to know what data is persisted in logs and for how long. Also KMS integration for Private deploys.
06:30 Jordan Lee: On Hosted we have a retention policy (default 30 days) and you can opt out of logging or obfuscate PII via a redact pipeline. For Private (VPC/on-prem) you control the logs and KMS. We have SOC 2 docs and an HSM/KMS integration guide we can share.
07:10 Dr. Kevin Wu: If we go Dedicated, can we pin model versions to avoid drift during clinical trials?
07:25 Priya Patel: Absolutely — per-cluster model pinning and rollout policies are first-class. The console shows current version, rollout percentage, and you can do canary or A/B.
08:00 Sara Morales: Walk me through an example of cost for summarize route.
08:08 Priya Patel: Sure — looking at a 30-day window: summarize has 18k requests, average tokens in = 420, tokens out = 1,200, total tokens 18k * 1620 = ~29M tokens. Based on rlm-7b-fp16 unit rate that maps to about $X — the console shows unit price per 1k tokens and route subtotal. Note the price varies if we route to cheaper quantized variants during off-peak.
09:05 Ravi Desai: Is that $X realistic? Our internal model estimates were lower. How much of that is infra overhead vs model compute?
09:20 Alex Chen: The cost shown includes model compute + amortized infra + caching savings. There's a breakdown: pure model vGPU time, per-instance overhead, and caching/batch savings. If you want a tailored number we can run a benchmark with your prompt set.
10:05 Priya Patel: I'll flag the benchmark runbook — it includes sample prompts, a way to collect representative traffic, and steps to run Redwood's perf harness. We'll show the same dashboards post-benchmark so you can compare.
11:30 Sara Morales: On routing: can we route by region and fall back to hosted if dedicated capacity is full?
11:45 Jordan Lee: Yes — Smart routing policies let you set priority order: dedicated pool, region X, fallback to hosted. The console will mark requests that took fallback and show the extra latency/cost.
12:20 Maya Singh: For PHI we need encryption in transit and at rest and audit logs immutable for 1 year — can Redwood support that for Private?
12:34 Alex Chen: For Private yes, full control; for Dedicated we can offer extended retention as an add-on and integrations with customer KMS. We'll send formal answers in the security pack.
13:02 Dr. Kevin Wu: A bit worried about token attribution accuracy. How do you handle split requests or streaming?
13:20 Priya Patel: Token attribution ties each generation call to a route and model. For streaming we record the final token counts and attribute them. There are edge cases (client-side concat) but we have heuristics and you can add metadata to calls to ensure correct attribution.
14:10 Sara Morales: Is there a way to set per-route budgets or alerts?
14:20 Priya Patel: Yes — Budgeting in Console lets you set monthly spend caps per route; when thresholds are hit you can auto-block or throttle. Alerts integrate with PagerDuty/Slack.
15:05 Ravi Desai: If we throttle, is there an option for queueing or graceful degradation?
15:18 Jordan Lee: We support graceful degradation: fallback to a smaller model variant, or return a cached summary, or queue with a short TTL — these are configurable per-route. The console will show the routing policy and recent decisions.
16:00 Alex Chen: Switching gears — we talked about per-token unit economics. For POC we usually recommend focusing on 3 routes and a month of traffic to get representative numbers. Pilot SOW will include benchmark runs, expected throughput, and a recommended deployment (hosted vs dedicated).
17:05 Sara Morales: Our infra team also wants to know the expected GPU footprint for the peak — can you show how the console estimates that?
17:20 Priya Patel: Sure — under Capacity Insights we show estimated concurrent tokens/sec and map that to instance types. Example: with your 95th percentile throughput we'd expect 4 x A100-equivalent nodes for rlm-7b-fp16 with a 20% buffer. There's a confidence band and we've found estimates are conservative.
18:10 Ravi Desai: Do you support multi-tenant isolation on Dedicated? We need strict per-team isolation.
18:25 Jordan Lee: Yes — Dedicated has namespace isolation and RBAC, plus VPC peering options. We can also do per-tenant clusters for stricter isolation.
19:05 Maya Singh: Any known compliance caveats?
19:12 Alex Chen: We'll share SOC 2, ISO attestation docs; for clinical data there are deployment patterns customers use — Private deploy or Dedicated with strict logging and KMS are most common.
20:00 Priya Patel: Back in the console — here's a per-route page for "eligibility-check" showing p50/p90 latency, cost per 1k tokens, percent of requests hitting cold start, and top error codes. You can filter by model, by version, and by time window.
21:10 Sara Morales: Are these dashboards customizable to add our own KPIs?
21:18 Jordan Lee: You can add computed metrics — e.g., cost per successful response — and surface them as columns. We also have a telemetry API to export metrics to Datadog or Prometheus.
22:05 Dr. Kevin Wu: For the trial, can Redwood run a bench and provide a cost projection and a regression check against our current model outputs?
22:20 Priya Patel: Yes — the Optimize toolkit will recommend quantization and batching profiles and will run evals on your gold set to check quality regressions. We'll include quality thresholds in the SOW.
23:05 Sara Morales: What's turnaround on that? We need results within two weeks for internal review.
23:15 Alex Chen: We can start the benchmark as soon as we have the prompt set and sample traffic; typical turnaround 7-10 days for the first pass.
24:00 Maya Singh: For SSO and RBAC — do you integrate with our Okta?
24:08 Jordan Lee: Yes — SAML/Okta supported for Console, plus SCIM for user provisioning.
25:00 Priya Patel: Quick note: the console shows historical cost per route and an anomaly detection that can flag spikes caused by model changes or a bad prompt.
25:35 Sara Morales: Hmm that's useful. We had a past incident where a prompt misconfiguration caused runaway tokens.
25:48 Alex Chen: The anomaly alert would have caught that — we'll show how to set those thresholds in the follow-up doc.
26:30 Ravi Desai: Can we export the whole dashboard as a snapshot for execs?
26:40 Priya Patel: Yes — PDF/CSV snapshots and scheduled reports are supported.
27:20 Dr. Kevin Wu: On pricing — will you provide committed pricing for Dedicated?
27:30 Alex Chen: For Dedicated we offer reserved capacity pricing + a monthly commitment. We'll include details in the pricing sheet. For Hosted the per-token pricing is usage-based; the console's predictive run-rate can help forecast spend under various scenarios.
28:15 Sara Morales: Any gotchas with quantized models around quality for clinical text?
28:28 Priya Patel: Quantization can sometimes affect subtle generation patterns. That's why Optimize runs evals and we recommend human-in-the-loop QA for clinical outputs. We'll set quality thresholds.
29:20 Alex Chen: Quick recap — action items: we'll send pricing/SOW, Priya shares benchmark runbook, customer shares prompt set and route list. We aim to kick off pilot first week of July.
29:50 Sara Morales: Sounds good. One last question: is there a plug-in or webhook to automatically tag requests with patient ID hashing?
30:05 Jordan Lee: You can pass metadata in the request and we support pre-request hooks for hashing or redaction; we'll share examples.
31:00 Maya Singh: Please add a note about data residency in the security doc — some PHI must remain in US regions.
31:12 Alex Chen: Noted, we'll include region constraints in SOW.
32:00 Priya Patel: Alright, i'll stop screen-sharing and Alex will run through next steps. Any final questions?
32:10 Dr. Kevin Wu: None from me.
32:15 Sara Morales: Nope. Thanks everyone.
32:20 Alex Chen: Thanks all. Recap: Alex send pricing + SOW (due 6/28), Priya send benchmark runbook (due 6/27), Ravi send routes and throughput targets (due 7/2), Maya send security questionnaire answers (due 6/29). We'll plan a POC kickoff w/c 2026-07-06.
41:50 Meeting ends

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels, filler words, and some proper nouns mis-transcribed (e.g., rlm model names may appear different).
